import pytest
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from subject import compute_freshness_score


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_same_time():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    score = compute_freshness_score(now, now)
    assert score == 1.0


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_future_created_at():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    future = now + timedelta(days=10)
    score = compute_freshness_score(future, now)
    # days_old is max(0, negative) -> 0, so score should be 1.0
    assert score == 1.0


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_one_week():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created = now - timedelta(days=7)
    score = compute_freshness_score(created, now)
    # e^(-0.015 * 7) = e^(-0.105) ≈ 0.9003
    expected = 0.9003
    assert abs(score - expected) < 0.001


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_four_weeks():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created = now - timedelta(days=28)
    score = compute_freshness_score(created, now)
    # e^(-0.015 * 28) = e^(-0.42) ≈ 0.6570
    expected = 0.6570
    assert abs(score - expected) < 0.001


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_eight_weeks():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created = now - timedelta(days=56)
    score = compute_freshness_score(created, now)
    # e^(-0.015 * 56) = e^(-0.84) ≈ 0.4317
    expected = 0.4317
    assert abs(score - expected) < 0.001


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_very_old():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created = now - timedelta(days=3650)  # 10 years
    score = compute_freshness_score(created, now)
    # e^(-0.015 * 3650) = e^(-54.75) ≈ 1.7e-24, effectively 0
    assert score < 1e-10


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_freshness_score_fractional_days():
    now = datetime(2025, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
    created = now - timedelta(hours=12)  # 0.5 days
    score = compute_freshness_score(created, now)
    # e^(-0.015 * 0.5) = e^(-0.0075) ≈ 0.9925
    expected = 0.9925
    assert abs(score - expected) < 0.001
